question: Is any buffer of the per-evaluation Metal SSB phase-loss pipeline byte-identical across different aberration triples, so that the work producing it could be hoisted out of the fit's 228 evaluations for a bit-exact speedup?

entrypoints: experiments/20260916-ssb-candidate-hoist/probe_hoist.swift (driver: real loss path, two candidates, one engine)
experiments/20260916-ssb-candidate-hoist/hoist-table.py (renders the candidate-independence table from a report)
code.note: probe-digest.patch adds an env-gated (SSB_PROBE_DIGEST=1) device digest kernel plus probeDumpDigests()/probeDigestKnownAnswer() accessors and records one digest per buffer write in the fused 512 loss path. It is scratch instrumentation and is NOT applied to the committed tree; the measured revision is 597b566 plus that patch.

parameters.digest: per-thread FNV-1a over 16 consecutive uint32 followed by a commutative 32-bit low/high pair reduction; validated against a host implementation of the same fold (known answer and mutation) and against an all-zero region

artifact_results.hoist-c1: Run 1: 21 buffer groups digested over 2 candidates. G cache (9 chunks), bfGeometry, twiddle, qRow, qCol identical across candidates; chiTrig, crossTrig, column-pass output (1118/1118 batches), Nyquist correction (1068/1118) and both moment accumulators differ. Losses 0.1376979947090149 (pinned optimum) and 0.13769979774951935. prepare 2.164 s, 11.37 GB allocated.
artifact_results.hoist-c2: Run 2 repeats run 1 in a fresh process: all 21 digest groups and both losses bit-identical, which is the reproducibility control for the table. prepare 2.256 s.
artifact_results.table: Rendered table plus the per-evaluation traffic split: 9.408 GB (33.0%) candidate-independent, 19.117 GB (67.0%) candidate-dependent, hoistable saving 0 B per evaluation.
artifact_results.log-c1: gpurun wrapper log for run 1: waited 78.2 s for the GPU lock, exit 0.
artifact_results.log-c2: gpurun wrapper log for run 2: waited 59.6 s for the GPU lock, exit 0.

execution.timing_caveat: digest dispatches add about 9.5 GB of device reads per evaluation, so the probe's wall seconds are not a timing result; use 267 ms/evaluation from the objective-profile experiment for timing.

outputs.result: Run 1 digests: G/geometry/twiddle identical, chi/cross/intermediate/Nyquist/moments differ. Losses 0.1376979947090149 and 0.13769979774951935.
Run 2 in a fresh process: every digest group and both losses bit-identical to run 1.
Buffer-by-buffer table and traffic split; 50 of 1118 Nyquist batches are an all-zero correction in both runs (host-side digest of a zero region matches exactly).
